what: [health] `fidelity: faithful` on a trend or pullback evidence record still does NOT mean the harness modelled the take-profit the leg actually has live. Live places `tp = min(entry*(1+0.099), entry + tp_r*risk)` -- the ~9.9 percent Bybit TP-distance clamp on the 50R sentinel -- and `regime_debt_matrix.build_harness_cmd` passes no `--tp-cap-pct`, so `tp_cap_pct` defaults to 0.0 and the harness has NO take-profit exit path at all. MEASURED 2026-09-22 by running the rerun command over config/strategies.yaml: 41 enabled legs route to trend or pullback, 28 of them carry `tp_r: 50.0`, every one declares some tp_r, and ZERO runs pass --tp-cap-pct. E46 (PI-20260922-E41-0005) made a BINDING declared tp_r (< 20R) count as an omitted lever, which took `faithful` from 37/52 to 25/52 enabled legs; the 28 sentinel legs were deliberately left `faithful` because a 50R target cannot be reached -- but the 9.9 percent CLAMP can, and at atr_stop_mult 2.5 with 2-3 percent ATR it lands at 1.3-2.0R, an ordinary frequently-touched target (scripts/backtest_trend.py's own comment). So every trail-family number in the corpus is measured on a book that cannot take profit. This is BL-20260810-BACKTEST-DOES-NOT-MODEL-THE-LIVE-CAPPED-TP reaching the evidence records; NOT folded into E46 because turning the cap on silently re-bases the whole fleet's history, which backtest_trend.py's own `--tp-cap-pct` default-off comment refuses in terms.
